name: Turn off debug output before production launch
query: We launch tomorrow. I enabled WP_DEBUG and WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY last week to chase down a plugin conflict and never turned them off — yesterday a visitor sent me a screenshot of a red PHP warning with file paths in it. Can you get the site's configuration production-ready?
expected_behavior: Locate the debug settings in wp-config.php and identify that WP_DEBUG and WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY are both true on a live site, leaking paths, queries, and secrets to visitors
Set define( 'WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY', false ) so errors are never rendered to visitors
Add @ini_set( 'display_errors', '0' ) as a server-level guard against display of errors
If debug logging is required, set define( 'WP_DEBUG_LOG', true ) only together with a server rule (Require all denied in .htaccess or deny all in nginx) blocking wp-content/debug.log from the web

While hardening wp-config.php, verify the companion production constants from the skill's reference: unique salts for all eight AUTH_KEY/AUTH_SALT through NONCE_KEY/NONCE_SALT values, DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT set to true, and FORCE_SSL_ADMIN set to true
Confirm least-privilege filesystem permissions: wp-config.php at 640/600, files 644, directories 755
Verify as an unauthenticated visitor that the previously reported page no longer renders any PHP errors or warnings
success_criteria: wp-config.php no longer defines WP_DEBUG as true with WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY as true; display of errors is disabled in production
If WP_DEBUG_LOG is enabled, a server rule blocks wp-content/debug.log from direct web access
The page that previously showed the PHP warning renders no error output to unauthenticated visitors
Companion hardening constants are present: unique salts, DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT true, FORCE_SSL_ADMIN true
wp-config.php permissions are restricted to 640 or 600
